sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Assen, the capital of Drenthe, charges for street parking in nine zones around the centre and wants to move cars into garages. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 18 December 2025, with amounts unchanged from 2025: 0.50 euro per 12 minutes, or 2.50 euros an hour, at street meters, and 0.30 euro per 10 minutes with a 6-euro daily maximum at Veemarktplein and part of Industrieweg [0]. Paid parking in zones 1 to 8 runs Monday to Saturday from 9:00 to 21:00 and Sunday from 12:00 to 18:00, and visitors without a permit may stay at most 120 minutes at a time; zone 9, Assen Oost, is paid Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 18:00; and in the inner city paid parking runs from 9:00 to 18:00, to 21:00 on Fridays [3]. A resident permit where meters apply costs 15.48 euros a month, and the additional assessment for unpaid parking costs 82 euros plus one hour of the local tariff [2]. A zero-emission zone for delivery vans and lorries has applied in the pedestrian inner city since 1 January 2025, enforced by cameras [9]. The Visie mobiliteit 2040, published on 17 July 2025, wants a ring road turned into a parking ring leading to garages, a Parkeerstrategie with area-based parking plans, a phased extension of regulated parking where pressure is high and simpler rules; these are intentions and not decisions on zones [6]. A list of council commitments of 16 January 2026 still shows three parking items as open, including the promised parking strategy [17].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Developments are small or in planning. The vision says the station could become the main mobility hub of Drenthe, with hubs also planned in Kloosterveen, Assen-Zuid and at bus station Marsdijk, and notes that scarce grid capacity poses major challenges for charging infrastructure [8]. The Structuurvisie Havenkwartier of May 2024 plans a low-car district near the station, with one parking space per dwelling, resident parking concentrated in collective facilities and a parking fund to which all building initiatives must contribute [16]. On 18 December 2025 the municipality published an application for an environmental permit to alter the parking garage at Doevenkamp 3, without details, and we do not know the outcome [11]. On 26 June 2026 the municipality designated two spaces near Vaart N.Z. 76 for charging only [10]. Its charging vision of February 2023 projected about 3,800 electric cars in 2025 and 9,000 in 2030, with a computed need of 190 and 465 public charging posts [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality owns the eight public garages, seven in the inner city and one in Kloosterveen, according to the charging vision of 2023, and for all of them the 2026 tariff is 0.50 euro per 15 minutes with an 8-euro daily maximum [13][1]. A monthly garage pass costs 37.50 euros for Assen residents, 68.50 euros for a worker pass and 80 euros for a pass for non-residents [1]. Q-Park lists the P+R at the station as its only car park in Assen, with 266 spaces, open round the clock, and no tariffs shown online [12]. The municipal parking monitor, quoted in the 2025 vision, found that on Saturday afternoons, the peak, about 450 garage spaces in the centre stay unused, and fewer than 400 of more than 800 on-street spaces are occupied [7]. A 2019 visitor survey found that, among visitors parking outside the garages, 41 percent used Mercuriusplein and 9 percent the P+R at the station, and it may no longer reflect current use [15].

Our data cover the P+R at the station, with 266 spaces, for about 60 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 24% on weekdays and 9% at weekends, which fits a commuter car park, and it peaked at 91% on a Thursday afternoon. The garages in the centre are not in our data.
